Maladaptive Strategies.value: I imagine getting revenge on the people responsible
constantly check body for signs of danger or injury
I detach myself from the memories

Threat.value: I often react as if I am in danger even when nothing is actually wrong
Sudden movements by others put me immediately on guard
I feel on guard even inside my own home

Memory.value: Something in my surroundings can instantly bring back the full memory without warning
When I try to explain what happened I lose the thread and cannot finish
When I have memories of what happened I sometimes hear things in my head that I heard during the frightening event.

Negative Appraisals.value: I acted in ways that go against who I am
Somebody else would have stopped the event from happening

vignette: Kwame, a 21-year-old African chef working at a bustling downtown restaurant, has been struggling with the aftermath of a sexual assault that occurred six months ago. The trauma of the event still haunts him daily, and he is seeking help as his coping mechanisms have begun to disrupt his life. The incident took place during a late-night shift when Kwame was alone in the kitchen. A former colleague who had been fired for harassment reappeared unexpectedly and attacked him. The sudden intrusion, combined with the loss of control and violence, created an indelible mark on his psyche. Since then, Kwame has found himself constantly scanning his environment for signs of danger. This heightened sense of vigilance was particularly triggered by car sounds outside the restaurant, which reminded him of the night when the former colleague arrived. Kwame’s triggers have led to a complex array of maladaptive strategies and thoughts. When he hears a car horn or an engine revving near his workplace, it often sets off a cascade of distressing memories. These auditory cues instantly bring back the full intensity of the assault, leaving him feeling on edge and vigilant even inside his own home. This heightened state of alertness has become a constant presence in Kwame’s life, making it difficult for him to relax or feel safe. One of Kwame's primary coping mechanisms is his intense preoccupation with revenge fantasies. He often imagines scenarios where he confronts the person responsible and exacts retribution. These thoughts provide a brief moment of relief from his anxiety but are ultimately unhelpful as they reinforce his sense of being constantly under threat. The cycle is self-perpetuating: his triggers lead to these violent imaginings, which in turn heighten his overall state of alertness. The memories themselves are fragmented and often come without warning. Kwame finds himself detached from the memory, almost as if it’s happening to someone else. He struggles to explain what happened clearly, losing the thread of his narrative when he tries to recount the event. This inability to process the trauma in a coherent way makes him feel even more isolated and unable to escape the memories. The assault has profoundly shaken Kwame's sense of self-worth and identity. He feels violated by the actions taken against him and believes that someone else would have been able to prevent what happened. These negative appraisals compound his distress, making it harder for him to move forward with a sense of hope. The feeling of hopelessness is deeply intertwined with his memories; he often finds himself questioning why he couldn't stop the assault, which further triggers intrusive thoughts and flashbacks. Kwame’s daily routine as a chef has become increasingly challenging. His preoccupation with revenge fantasies and constant body monitoring distract him from his work, leading to mistakes that have affected his job performance. He feels that every sudden movement by his coworkers puts him on guard, making it hard for him to focus or build relationships in the kitchen. The assault's lasting impact is evident in Kwame’s growing sense of isolation and distress. What frightened him most was not just the physical violence but the loss of control over his own body and environment. This has made everyday sounds and movements potent triggers that continuously remind him of the trauma. The cumulative effect of these symptoms has led to a significant decrease in his quality of life, affecting both his work and personal well-being. Kwame finally decided to seek help after a particularly distressing incident where he had a panic attack at work, unable to control his reactions when a car outside blared its horn loudly. He recognized that the cycle of triggers, maladaptive strategies, and negative appraisals was becoming unsustainable. Kwame hopes for some relief from these overwhelming memories and a way to reclaim his sense of self-worth and identity without being haunted by the past.
